newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on slack exports, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on slack exports, weather.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a lack of significant export business and weather patterns viewed as overall conducive for the U.S. winter wheat crop, traders said.
But wheat remained underpinned by another rally in the soybean pit.
"Wheat and corn are just going along for the ride," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Soybeans Wednesday rallied to contract highs with a threatened port strike in Brazil cited as a key contributer to the advances.
There also was talk of cuts in production forecasts for the Brazilian soy crop and talk China bought a cargo of soybeans for spot shipment.
But uncertainty about weather patterns in portions of the U.S. wheat growing region also circulated through the pit.
Less-than-expected rainfall overnight in portions of Kansas lent support to new crop July but forecasts for more rain limited bullish enthusiasm.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed four to six cents per bushel lower, with May down 5-1/4 at $3.88-1/2 a bushel. New crop July closed 4-3/4 cents lower at $3.86.

Agronomists this week said the HRW crop was in overall good condition and in the soft red winter wheat states the extension agronomists this week said only minor amounts of wheat was damaged recently by flooding in Ohio.
But they said Wednesday that Indiana's soft red winter wheat crop was showing early signs of disease, and agronomists fear continued wet weather will hasten outbreaks and reduce yields.
The four- and 20-day moving averages (MA) for the May contract were giving off bullish signals early Wednesday. The four-day MA for May was at $3.97 and the 20-day was at $3.85.

Technicians said first support in the May was at $3.88-1/2 and second support was at $3.74. The session low for May was $3.86. First resistance was at $4.03 and second resistance was at $4.17-1/2. The session high for May was $3.93-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 54 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

Term Commodities sold one million bushels of July and Smith Barney sold 1.5 million July, traders said. LIT America bought 1.5 million bushels of July, SAK Futures bought and sold two million bushesl of July.
Refco Inc bought two million bushels of July, traders said, and Continental Grain bear spread 2.2 million bushels of September/July at 2-1/2 cents, premium September.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 23,000 contracts, above the 22,007 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 May $3.90 calls at 8-3/4 cents and sold 400 May $4.00 calls at five cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 9,284 traded Tuesday.
